Ewan Ross-Murray | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source The reverse fixture was won by the Red Devils. | Massimo Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio/Getty Images Everything is on the line when Belgium hosts Italy in Sunday’s all-or-nothing UEFA Nations League group stage clash. 
--> Everything is on the line when Belgium hosts Italy in Sunday’s all-or-nothing UEFA Nations League group stage clash. 
 The European giants both harbor ambitions of reaching next year’s quarterfinals, and it’s the Azzurri currently in the driving seat. Italy must simply avoid defeat at Stade Roi Baudouin to progress in one of the top two positions, although victory would guarantee first place courtesy of a superior head-to-head record with chasers France. 
--> The European giants both harbor ambitions of reaching next year’s quarterfinals, and it’s the Azzurri currently in the driving seat. Italy must simply avoid defeat at Stade Roi Baudouin to progress in one of the top two positions, although victory would guarantee first place courtesy of a superior head-to-head record with chasers France. 
 Things are slightly more complicated for Belgium in Group A1, however, as it needs to claim all three points to ensure a spot in the last eight. Victory combined with France dropping points at home against Türkiye would see the Red Devils finish first.
--> Things are slightly more complicated for Belgium in Group A1, however, as it needs to claim all three points to ensure a spot in the last eight. Victory combined with France dropping points at home against Türkiye would see the Red Devils finish first.
 Roberto Mancini’s return to the Italy dugout has coincided with an upturn in form, underscored by the recent 3–1 win over France. However, his side did lose to Belgium in the reverse fixture in September, which finished 2–0 to Mark van Bommel on his dugout debut.
